correctness.rationale: Reversibility makes \(A=-Q+D\) self-adjoint in \(L^2(\pi)\), and its Dirichlet-form decomposition is strictly positive under irreducibility and positive mean event rate. The spectral theorem therefore represents the time-stationary survival as a positive finite mixture of exponentials. Its hazard derivative is exactly minus the variance of the spectral rates under exponentially tilted weights. The initial hazard is \(\lambda_*\), while self-adjointness gives the exact identity \(S_\alpha=-S_\pi'/\lambda_*\). These facts prove \(S_\alpha\le S_\pi\). Equality analysis is exact because zero spectral variance means \(\mathbf 1\) is an eigenvector of \(A\), equivalently \(D\mathbf 1\) is constant, so all event rates are equal.

originality.rationale: The motivating paper states the time-stationary versus event-stationary survival inequality as a conjecture for irreducible MMPPs, proves the two-state case, and notes the symmetric-C subclass. Reversibility with nonuniform stationary distribution is strictly broader than ordinary matrix symmetry, and the weighted-space proof is not implied by simply symmetrizing the matrix because the similarity transform generally does not preserve the Markov all-ones structure. value.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly identifies the stochastic order as a central MMPP problem. Reversibility is a major structural class that includes every finite birth-death modulator and many nonsymmetric generators with nonuniform stationary laws. The finding gives the full survival-function order, strictness/equality characterization, and an additional hyperexponential/decreasing-hazard representation, so it is a substantive structural advance beyond a scalar moment bound or a narrow numerical example.
